land.text: the western half of the Chagatai ulus, ruled by Qazan Khan until 1346

predecessors.note: Cliopatria keeps one Chagatai Khanate row to 1462; the chagatai-khanate dossier records the 1346 split with this slug as counterpart.

land.text: Transoxiana and Balkh, where Timur was crowned in April 1370

successors.note: Timur and Husayn shared the state 1363-1370 (Chagatai page).

capitals.name: Qarshi (Nakhshab)
capitals.note: The Chagatai Khanate infobox lists capitals Almaliq and Qarshi; Qarshi is the Transoxiana seat. No page opened names Qazaghan's, Husayn's or Timur's seat before 1370 (Timur's Samarkand is called 'his capital' without a date).

rulers.name: Qazaghan
rulers.title: amir
rulers.note: Amir of the Qara'unas 'from 1345 at the latest'; assassinated 1358. Puppet khans: Danishmendji 1346-1348, Bayan Quli 1348-1358 (Qazaghan page).

rulers.name: Abdullah
rulers.title: amir
rulers.note: Succeeded his father; in 1358 he killed Bayan Quli and was driven out by Hajji Beg (Chagatai page).

rulers.name: Hajji Beg and Bayan Selduz
rulers.title: amirs
rulers.note: They 'split Transoxiana' until Tughlugh Timur's invasion of 1360; Hajji Beg was Timur's uncle.

rulers.name: Amir Husayn and Timur
rulers.title: amirs
rulers.note: After Tughlugh Timur's death in 1363 'Timur and Amir Husayn took over Transoxiana'; Timur eliminated Husayn about 1370.

correction.text: Transoxania: 'Transoxania was ruled by Qazan Khan ibn Yasaur' until Qazaghan killed him in 1346

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row (Cliopatria's Chagatai Khanate row carries the whole western ulus until 1462, and Moghulistan the east from 1463). The pages give Transoxiana as the western half and say Qazaghan 'mainly commanded the loyalty of the southern tribes'; they do not list Balkh, Badakhshan or Khorasan as his. Herat was a tributary from 1351 (vassal event), not territory. No infobox area exists. [Reviewer ia-02-x, 2026-10-19] to 1359->1360: no keyframe covered 1360, the year of the Moghul invasion (contest_start); Transoxiana is lost only in 1361 (ledger).

correction.text: the remnant of Husayn's following in Afghanistan after Tughlugh Timur had 'defeated Amir Husayn in Afghanistan'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, low certainty: with Transoxiana under Tughlugh Timur the pages leave only Husayn in Afghanistan, with no place named; Balkh is the reading from Timur's later puppet khan at Balkh. A gap-filler could drop this keyframe and draw nothing for 1361-1362.

correction.text: Transoxiana and Balkh: 'Following Tughlugh's death in 1363, Timur and Amir Husayn took over Transoxiana'; Timur 'gained control of the western Chagatai Khanate by 1370' with a puppet khan at Balkh

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Balkh is where Timur was crowned on 9 April 1370 and set up Suyurghatmish; the pages do not say when Husayn took it.

region.text: Transoxania, the western half of the Chagatai ulus

ledger.note: 1346: Amir Qazaghan kills Qazan Khan and rules Transoxiana. 'Transoxania was ruled by Qazan Khan ibn Yasaur. In 1346 a tribal chief, Amir Qazaghan, killed Qazan' and installed Danishmendji as puppet khan; the Qazaghan page: 'Qazan's death signified the end of the effective power of the Chagatai khans within the ulus'.

1351: Herat pays tribute to Qazaghan. Qazaghan 'made Herat a tributary in 1351'; the Qazaghan page has him lead a coalition that sacked Herat after Arlat and Arpardi complaints of Kartid raids (no year).
1358: Qazaghan is assassinated by the son of Borolday and Herat's tribute ends with him; neither page says when it stopped.

1360: Tughlugh Timur invades Transoxiana. 'In 1360, Tughlugh invaded Transoxania and conquered it'; Timur joined him and was made ruler of Shahr-i Sebz; Hajji Beg returned and was driven off again, killed near Sebzewar.

1361: Transoxiana is lost. The Chagatai page says Tughlugh 'conquered it' in 1360 and then 'defeated Amir Husayn in Afghanistan'; the chagatai-khanate dossier dates the decisive second invasion to 1361. The decisive year is the researcher's reading.
1361: Transoxiana goes to Moghulistan under Tughlugh Timur and then Ilyas Khoja; only Husayn's following in Afghanistan remains.

1363: Timur and Amir Husayn retake Transoxiana. 'Following Tughlugh's death in 1363, Timur and Amir Husayn took over Transoxiana'; they forced Ilyas Khoja out, beat him on the Syr Darya in 1364 and he retreated in 1365 after an epidemic.

9 April 1370: Timur is crowned at Balkh. Infobox 'Coronation: 9 April 1370, Balkh'; 'Around 1370, Husayn surrendered to Timur and was later assassinated'; Timur 'gained control of the western Chagatai Khanate by 1370'. The Timurid Empire begins (timurid-empire dossier, April 1370).

wars.name: Moghul conquest of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Tughlugh Timur of Moghulistan invaded in 1360 and 'conquered it'; Hajji Beg was killed near Sebzewar and Husayn beaten in Afghanistan. Timur served Tughlugh and was made ruler of Shahr-i Sebz.
wars.note: The chagatai-khanate dossier dates the contest March 1360 to 1361 and the Moghul hold to 1363.

wars.name: Qazaghan’s sack of Herat
wars.outcome: Qazaghan 'made Herat a tributary in 1351' and led a coalition that sacked it in the 1350s; no land was annexed.

wars.name: Timur and Husayn against Ilyas Khoja
wars.outcome: Ilyas Khoja 'attacked Timur in 1364 and was defeated on the Syr Darya', retreating the next year after an epidemic; Transoxiana stayed with Timur and Husayn.

certainty.note: Oasis and steppe frontiers; the pages give no line for any of the three phases.

sources.title: Qazaghan
sources.note: Qazaghan: Qara'unas amir from 1345, killed Qazan 1346, puppet khans Danishmendji 1346-48 and Bayan Quli 1348-58, Herat sacked in the 1350s, assassinated 1358, son Abdullah succeeded.

sources.title: Chagatai Khanate
sources.note: 1346 killing of Qazan; Herat tributary 1351; 1358 Abdullah and Hajji Beg; Tughlugh Timur conquers Transoxania 1360; Timur and Husayn take over after 1363; Ilyas Khoja 1364; infobox capitals Almaliq and Qarshi.

sources.title: Timur
sources.note: Timur: coronation 9 April 1370 at Balkh, Husayn surrendered and was assassinated c.1370, western Chagatai Khanate under control by 1370, puppet khan Suyurghatmish at Balkh.

notes:
The western half of the Chagatai ulus between the death of Qazan Khan (1346) and Timur's coronation (April 1370). Cliopatria draws the whole of the Chagatai Khanate as one row to 1462, so no shape exists; the chagatai-khanate dossier (ia-02-a) already uses the slug amirate-of-qazaghan as the counterpart of its 1346 split, its 1360-1361 contest and its 1363 loss, and this dossier mirrors those events.

Territory is thin: the pages name Transoxania as the western half (Chagatai page) but not Fergana, Badakhshan, Balkh or Khorasan; Qazaghan 'mainly commanded the loyalty of the southern tribes' (Qazaghan page). Herat was a tributary in 1351-1358. The 1361-1362 keyframe is a bridge. The Chagatai page puts the conquest of Transoxania in 1360 and Timur's takeover at 'Following Tughlugh's death in 1363' and gives 1369 for his mastery; the Timur page gives 9 April 1370; the chagatai-khanate dossier dates a second Moghul invasion to 1361 and Husayn's death to 1370.

Not drawn: the Sarbadar and Kartid wars of the 1350s (Qazaghan page, undated), Qazaghan's raid on northern India and his aid to Muhammad bin Tughluq in 1350/51 (no land), and the Husayn-Timur quarrel of 1368-1370 (undated on the Timur page).
